Example: an input of [1, 35, 12, 10] returns ["Large breed formula", "Add joint support vitamins", "Reduce daily caloric intake"].

title: Real Estate Valuer
spec: Write a function `value(property)` that provides a property assessment. The input is a list of four numbers: distance to city center, building age, room count, and plot size. Return a list of string observations. If distance is below five, add "Prime central location". If distance is above twenty, add "Suburban or rural setting". If age is below five, add "Modern construction". If age is above fifty, add "Historic property charm". If room count is below three, add "Suitable for singles or couples". If room count is above six, add "Ideal for large families". If plot size is below two hundred, add "Low maintenance yard". If plot size is above one thousand, add "Extensive outdoor space". If distance is below ten and age is below ten, add "Premium market value expected", otherwise add "Standard market valuation". Example: an input of [3, 2, 2, 150] returns ["Prime central location", "Modern construction", "Suitable for singles or couples", "Low maintenance yard", "Premium market value expected"].

title: Biking Route Generator
spec: Write a function `route(conditions)` that describes a cycling trip. The input is a list of four numbers: total distance, elevation gain, surface code (one for paved, two for gravel), and traffic density percentage. Return a list of string statements. If distance is above fifty, add "Bring plenty of hydration". If distance is below ten, add "Short casual ride". If elevation is above one thousand, add "Prepare for steep climbs". If elevation is below one hundred, add "Mostly flat terrain". If surface code is one, add "Road bike recommended". If surface code is two, add "Gravel or mountain bike needed". If traffic is above eighty, add "Wear high visibility clothing". If traffic is below twenty, add "Enjoy the quiet roads". If distance is above fifty and surface code is two, add "Epic challenge ahead", otherwise add "Have a safe ride". Example: an input of [60, 1200, 2, 90] returns ["Bring plenty of hydration", "Prepare for steep climbs", "Gravel or mountain bike needed", "Wear high visibility clothing", "Epic challenge ahead"].

title: Personal Finance Budgeter
spec: Write a function `budget(finances)` that reviews a monthly financial plan. The input is a list of four numbers: monthly income, fixed expenses, variable expenses, and a savings goal. Return a list of string alerts. If fixed expenses exceed half of the income, add "Fixed costs are too high". If fixed expenses are below a quarter of the income, add "Excellent fixed cost ratio". If variable expenses exceed the savings goal, add "Cut back on discretionary spending". If variable expenses are below the savings goal, add "Good control over daily spending". If the sum of both expenses exceeds the income, add "Warning negative cash flow". If the sum of both expenses is less than half of the income, add "Aggressive savings possible". If the savings goal is above one thousand, add "Ambitious saving target". If the savings goal is below one hundred, add "Consider increasing savings rate". If the income is greater than the sum of all expenses and the savings goal combined, add "Budget is well balanced". Example: an input of [5000, 3000, 1500, 1000] returns ["Fixed costs are too high", "Cut back on discretionary spending", "Ambitious saving target"].

title: Baking Conditions Adjuster
spec: Write a function `adjust(factors)` that tweaks a recipe for environmental conditions. The input is a list of four numbers: altitude in meters, humidity percentage, desired servings, and original flour weight in grams. Return a list of string directions. If altitude is above one thousand, add "Increase liquid ingredients slightly". If altitude is above two thousand, add "Decrease baking powder". If humidity is above seventy, add "Reduce water to prevent sticky dough". If humidity is below thirty, add "Cover dough to prevent drying out". If servings are above twenty, add "Bake in multiple batches". If servings are below five, add "Use a small baking pan". If original flour weight is above five hundred, add "Use a heavy duty stand mixer". If original flour weight is below two hundred, add "Mix by hand easily". If altitude is above one thousand and humidity is below thirty, add "Keep a close eye on baking time". Example: an input of [2500, 20, 25, 600] returns ["Increase liquid ingredients slightly", "Decrease baking powder", "Cover dough to prevent drying out", "Bake in multiple batches", "Use a heavy duty stand mixer", "Keep a close eye on baking time"].

title: Earth Composition Analyzer
spec: Write a function `analyze(soil)` that evaluates earth quality for planting. The input is a list of four numbers: clay percentage, sand percentage, silt percentage, and organic matter percentage. Return a list of string properties. If clay is above forty, add "Heavy soil requires aeration". If clay is below ten, add "Low clay content". If sand is above fifty, add "Fast draining soil". If sand is below twenty, add "Poor drainage expected". If silt is above fifty, add "High erosion risk". If silt is below twenty, add "Stable aggregate structure". If organic matter is below three, add "Incorporate compost immediately". If organic matter is above ten, add "Rich fertile ground". If the sum of clay, sand, and silt is exactly one hundred, add "Valid mineral composition", otherwise add "Invalid percentage totals". Example: an input of [50, 30, 20, 2] returns ["Heavy soil requires aeration", "Stable aggregate structure", "Incorporate compost immediately", "Valid mineral composition"].

title: Hiking Gear Recommender
spec: Write a function `pack(trip)` that lists equipment for a trek. The input is a list of four numbers: forecasted temperature, rain probability percentage, hike duration in hours, and backpack capacity in liters. Return a list of string items. If temperature is below ten, add "Pack thermal base layers". If temperature is above thirty, add "Bring extra sun protection". If rain probability is above fifty, add "Include waterproof jacket". If rain probability is below ten, add "Clear skies expected". If duration is above eight, add "Carry a water filter". If duration is below three, add "Small daypack is sufficient". If capacity is below twenty, add "Travel light and fast". If capacity is above fifty, add "Plenty of room for extras". If duration is above eight and rain probability is above fifty, add "Prepare for challenging conditions". Example: an input of [5, 80, 10, 60] returns ["Pack thermal base layers", "Include waterproof jacket", "Carry a water filter", "Plenty of room for extras", "Prepare for challenging conditions"].

title: PC Hardware Evaluator
spec: Write a function `verify(system)` that reviews pc specifications. The input is a list of four numbers: memory amount in gigabytes, processor cores, storage space in gigabytes, and graphics memory. Return a list of string evaluations. If memory amount is below eight, add "Upgrade memory for better multitasking". If memory amount is above thirty two, add "Sufficient memory for heavy workloads". If processor cores are below four, add "Basic computing only". If processor cores are above eight, add "Excellent processing power". If storage space is below two hundred, add "Free up disk space soon". If storage space is above one thousand, add "Plenty of storage available". If graphics memory is below two, add "Not suitable for modern gaming". If graphics memory is above eight, add "Ready for high resolution graphics". If memory is above sixteen, cores above six, and graphics above six, add "High end workstation detected". Example: an input of [4, 2, 150, 1] returns ["Upgrade memory for better multitasking", "Basic computing only", "Free up disk space soon", "Not suitable for modern gaming"].

title: Swimming Pool Chemical Balancer
spec: Write a function `balance(readings)` that prescribes water treatments. The input is a list of four numbers: chlorine level, acidity level, total alkalinity, and calcium hardness. Return a list of string actions. If chlorine is below two, add "Add chlorine shock". If chlorine is above five, add "Wait before swimming". If acidity is below seven, add "Broadcast soda ash". If acidity is above eight, add "Pour muriatic acid". If alkalinity is below eighty, add "Add baking soda". If alkalinity is above one hundred and twenty, add "Add dry acid". If calcium hardness is below two hundred, add "Dissolve calcium chloride". If calcium hardness is above four hundred, add "Partially drain and refill pool". If all four values fall within the normal ranges (chlorine two to five, acidity seven to eight, alkalinity eighty to one hundred twenty, calcium two hundred to four hundred inclusive), add "Water is perfectly balanced". Example: an input of [1, 6, 70, 150] returns ["Add chlorine shock", "Broadcast soda ash", "Add baking soda", "Dissolve calcium chloride"].

title: String Gauge Selector
spec: Write a function `select(guitar)` that chooses strings for a guitar. The input is a list of four numbers: scale length in inches, tuning pitch offset, player strength score, and fret wear score. Return a list of string suggestions. If scale length is below twenty four, add "Use thicker strings for tension". If scale length is above twenty six, add "Consider lighter gauge strings". If tuning pitch offset is below zero, add "Heavy bottom strings needed". If tuning pitch offset is above zero, add "Extra light strings required". If player strength is below five, add "Low tension silk and steel". If player strength is above eight, add "High tension bronze". If fret wear is above seven, add "Use flatwound strings to reduce wear". If fret wear is below three, add "Roundwound strings are fine". If player strength is above eight and tuning pitch offset is below zero, add "Custom hybrid set recommended". Example: an input of [23, -1, 9, 8] returns ["Use thicker strings for tension", "Heavy bottom strings needed", "High tension bronze", "Use flatwound strings to reduce wear", "Custom hybrid set recommended"].

title: Telescope Viewing Conditions
spec: Write a function `observe(weather)` that assesses the night sky. The input is a list of four numbers: cloud cover percentage, atmospheric seeing score, moon phase day, and light pollution index. Return a list of string observations. If cloud cover is above fifty, add "Too cloudy for observation". If cloud cover is below ten, add "Clear skies for astronomy". If atmospheric seeing is below four, add "Poor atmospheric stability". If it is above eight, add "Crisp planetary views possible". If moon phase day is above ten, add "Moonlight will wash out deep sky objects". If it is below four, add "Dark sky ideal for galaxies". If light pollution is above seven, add "Use narrowband filters". If it is below three, add "Pristine dark sky site". If cloud cover is below ten, seeing is above eight, moon is below four, and pollution is below three, add "Perfect night for astrophotography". Example: an input of [5, 9, 2, 2] returns ["Clear skies for astronomy", "Crisp planetary views possible", "Dark sky ideal for galaxies", "Pristine dark sky site", "Perfect night for astrophotography"].

title: Canvas Paint Mixer
spec: Write a function `mix(colors)` that analyzes a color combination. The input is a list of four numbers representing color amounts: red, blue, yellow, and white. Return a list of string results. If red is above fifty and blue is above fifty, add "Produces a dark purple". If red is above fifty and yellow is above fifty, add "Produces a bright orange". If blue is above fifty and yellow is above fifty, add "Produces a vibrant green". If red, blue, and yellow are all above fifty, add "Results in a muddy brown". If red is below ten and blue is below ten, add "Lacks cool tones". If white is above eighty, add "Creates a very pale pastel". If white is below ten, add "Deep saturated color". If red, blue, and yellow are all exactly zero, add "Pure white paint". If blue is strictly greater than zero and both red and yellow are zero, add "Monochromatic blue scheme". Example: an input of [60, 60, 60, 5] returns ["Produces a dark purple", "Produces a bright orange", "Produces a vibrant green", "Results in a muddy brown", "Deep saturated color"].

title: Drone Flight Prep
spec: Write a function `prepare(status)` that runs a preflight check. The input is a list of four numbers: battery percentage, available satellites, wind speed, and distance to the nearest airport. Return a list of string messages. If battery is below thirty, add "Charge battery before takeoff". If battery is above ninety, add "Battery fully ready". If satellites are below eight, add "Wait for better satellite lock". If satellites are above twelve, add "Strong location positioning". If wind speed is above twenty, add "Wind too strong for safe flight". If wind speed is below five, add "Calm air conditions". If distance is below five, add "Flight prohibited in this zone". If distance is above twenty, add "Clear of controlled airspace". If battery is above eighty, satellites above ten, wind below ten, and distance above ten, add "Ready for safe autonomous flight". Example: an input of [95, 14, 2, 25] returns ["Battery fully ready", "Strong location positioning", "Calm air conditions", "Clear of controlled airspace", "Ready for safe autonomous flight"].

title: Office Plant Care
spec: Write a function `water(plants)` that checks indoor greenery. The input is a list of lists, where each inner list contains three numbers for a plant: soil moisture percentage, days since last watered, and a leaf yellowing flag (zero or one). Return a list of string instructions. For each plant, evaluate the following: if moisture is below twenty, add "Needs immediate watering". If moisture is above eighty, add "Soil is waterlogged". If days since last watered is above fourteen, add "Check for dry rot". If days since last watered is below two, add "Recently watered". If the yellowing flag is one, add "Reduce sunlight exposure". If the yellowing flag is zero, add "Foliage looks healthy". After processing all plants, if more than three plants needed immediate watering, append "Schedule an office watering day" to the result. If none needed watering, append "All plants are hydrated". Example: an input of [[15, 15, 1], [85, 1, 0]] returns ["Needs immediate watering", "Check for dry rot", "Reduce sunlight exposure", "Soil is waterlogged", "Recently watered", "Foliage looks healthy"].

title: Dough Proofing Monitor
spec: Write a function `ferment(dough)` that monitors baking progress. The input is a list of four numbers: ambient temperature, yeast amount, hydration percentage, and resting time in hours. Return a list of string updates. If temperature is below eighteen, add "Fermentation will be sluggish". If temperature is above twenty eight, add "Watch for overproofing". If yeast amount is below two, add "Requires a long cold proof". If yeast amount is above five, add "Fast rise expected". If hydration is below sixty, add "Stiff dough for shaping". If hydration is above eighty, add "Sticky dough requires folding". If resting time is below two, add "Insufficient gluten development". If resting time is above twelve, add "Complex flavors developed". If temperature is above twenty five and yeast is above four, add "Punch down dough soon". Example: an input of [15, 1, 55, 1] returns ["Fermentation will be sluggish", "Requires a long cold proof", "Stiff dough for shaping", "Insufficient gluten development"].

title: Snowboard Tuning Shop
spec: Write a function `tune(skis)` that determines snow equipment service. The input is a list of four numbers: side edge angle, base damage score, wax temperature rating, and snow condition code (one for icy, two for slushy). Return a list of string services. If edge angle is below eighty eight, add "Aggressive race tune". If edge angle is above ninety, add "Forgiving recreational tune". If base damage score is above five, add "Requires core repair". If base damage score is exactly zero, add "Base is pristine". If wax temperature rating is below minus ten, add "Cold weather wax applied". If wax temperature rating is above zero, add "Warm spring wax needed". If snow condition code is one, add "Sharpen edges extra keen". If snow condition code is two, add "Apply structured base finish". If base damage is above five and condition code is one, add "Full base grind recommended". Example: an input of [87, 6, -15, 1] returns ["Aggressive race tune", "Requires core repair", "Cold weather wax applied", "Sharpen edges extra keen", "Full base grind recommended"].

title: Invoice Receipt Generator
spec: Write a function `invoice(items)` that takes a list of arrays, where each array contains an item name, a category word, and a number representing the base price. Loop through the items to calculate taxes. If the category is food, the tax is zero. If electronics, the tax is twenty percent. If clothing, the tax is ten percent. If books, the tax is five percent. If furniture, the tax is fifteen percent. Output an array of formatted strings where each string contains the item name, followed by a space and a dash and a space, the base price, the word plus, and the calculated tax amount. Append a final string to the array that says grand total followed by a colon and the sum of all prices and taxes. For example, an input of food apple two and books novel ten should result in strings like apple - two plus zero, novel - ten plus zero point five, and grand total: twelve point five.

title: Library Catalog Formatter
spec: Implement a function `bibliography(books)` that receives a list of arrays containing author name, publication year, title, publisher, and media format. Iterate through the list to generate formatted citation strings. If the media format is print, format the string as the author, a dot and space, the year wrapped in parentheses, a dot and space, the title wrapped in HTML italic tags, a dot and space, the publisher, a dot and space, and the word Print. If the format is digital, use the same structure but end with the word Web. If the format is audio, end with the word Audiobook. Return a single large string containing all citations separated by newline characters. For example, giving an array with Smith, two thousand, My Life, Acme Corp, print should output Smith. (2000). My Life. Acme Corp. Print.

title: Menu Markdown Builder
spec: Create a function `menu(dishes)` that takes a list of arrays where each array holds a dish name, a section name, and a numeric price. Group the dishes by their section. For the appetizers section, output a markdown heading consisting of two hash symbols, a space, and the word Appetizers. Repeat this heading pattern for mains, desserts, and beverages sections if they exist. Under each heading, format each dish on its own line as a bulleted list using a hyphen, a space, the dish name, a colon, a space, a dollar sign, and the price. Return the complete formatted markdown string with items separated by newlines. For example, an input with soup, appetizers, five should include a heading for appetizers and a line like - soup: $5.

title: Log File Parser
spec: Develop a function `parse(logs)` that accepts a list of string messages from a system server. Read each log line and categorize it based on specific keywords to generate a list of alert sentences. If the line contains the word FATAL, prepend the phrase CRITICAL ALERT followed by a colon and a space to the line. If it contains ERROR, prepend WARNING. If it contains WARN, prepend ATTENTION. If it contains INFO, prepend NOTICE. If it contains DEBUG, skip the line entirely and do not add it to the results. Return an array of the newly formatted string messages. For example, an input list with FATAL system crash and DEBUG variable x is two should return an array with just CRITICAL ALERT: FATAL system crash.

title: Resume Text Exporter
spec: Write a function `resume(details)` that accepts a list containing a person name string, a list of contact email strings, and a list of past job titles. Build and return a plain text resume layout as a single string. Start with the name centered by prepending four spaces, followed by a newline character. Then add a section header titled CONTACT INFO, followed by newlines and the emails formatted as bullet points with an asterisk and a space. Next, add a section header titled WORK EXPERIENCE, followed by the job titles prefixed with a plus sign and a space. Add a final section header titled EDUCATION at the bottom. The headers, spaces, symbols, and newlines will build a structured document. For example, John Doe with email john at mail and job clerk should output the centered name, the contact info section, the work experience section with clerk, and the education section.

title: SQL Insert Builder
spec: Create a function `insert(records)` that takes a list of arrays, where each inner array contains a user name string, an email string, and an age number. Construct SQL insert statements for a database table named users. Begin each statement with the exact phrase insert into users values open parenthesis. Format the name wrapped in single quotes, followed by a comma and a space, the email wrapped in single quotes, followed by another comma and space, and finally the age number without any quotes. Close the statement with a parenthesis and a semicolon. Return a list of these SQL strings. For example, an input with Bob, bob at mail, thirty should return insert into users values ('Bob', 'bob at mail', 30);

title: HTML Table Generator
spec: Implement a function `table(rows)` that receives a list of arrays, where the first array represents column headers and the subsequent arrays represent data rows. Create an HTML table string. Start the string with an open table tag. Open a table row tag, wrap each header item in open and close table header tags, and close the table row. For every remaining data array, open a table row tag, wrap each data item in open and close table data tags, and close the table row tag. Finish by appending a close table tag. Return the complete HTML string. For example, headers name and age with data Alice and ten should generate the corresponding HTML table structure.

title: XML Sitemap Creator
spec: Develop a function `sitemap(pages)` that accepts a list of arrays containing a web path, a frequency word, and a priority number. Build a search engine XML document as a single string. Begin the string with an xml version declaration and an open urlset tag. For each page in the list, append an open url tag. Inside it, append an open loc tag, a domain prefix of www dot example dot com, the path, and a close loc tag. Then append an open changefreq tag, the frequency word, and a close changefreq tag. Finally, append an open priority tag, the priority number, and a close priority tag. Close the url tag. After the loop, append a close urlset tag and return the final string. For example, path home with frequency daily and priority one should produce an XML block with those values nested inside urlset and url tags.

title: BBCode Forum Formatter
spec: Write a function `format(posts)` that takes a list of text strings containing custom forum bracket tags. Replace specific bracketed tags with their corresponding HTML equivalents. Replace every instance of open bracket b close bracket with an open strong tag, and the slash b version with a close strong tag. Replace the i tag with em tags. Replace the u tag with an open span style equals text decoration underline tag, and its closing tag with a close span tag. Replace the quote tag with blockquote tags. Return a new list of the converted HTML strings. For example, a post reading this is bracket b bold bracket slash b should return this is strong bold close strong.

title: Data Exporter
spec: Implement a function `export(rows)` that takes a list of arrays containing mixed data types like booleans, nulls, numbers, and strings. Convert the data to a custom text format. Start the final output string with the phrase DATA START followed by a newline. Loop over each row. If a value is the boolean true, output the word YES. If false, output NO. If null, output EMPTY. If it is a string, wrap it in double asterisks. Join the formatted values in each row with a pipe character enclosed by spaces. Join all the rows with a newline character. Append a newline and the phrase DATA END to the bottom. Return the resulting string. For example, a row with true, null, and text should output YES pipe EMPTY pipe double asterisk text double asterisk.

title: Chatbot Reply Generator
spec: Create a function `reply(intents)` that takes a list of intent category words from a user. Map each intent to a specific natural language sentence. If the intent is greeting, output hello, how can I help you today. If it is farewell, output goodbye and have a great day. If it is status, output your order is currently being processed. If it is refund, output your refund has been issued and will appear soon. If it is complaint, output we apologize for the inconvenience, let me connect you to an agent. If the intent does not match these, output I did not understand that command. Return a list of these exact sentence strings in order.

title: Markdown Calendar Builder
spec: Write a function `calendar(start, days)` that accepts an integer for the starting weekday, where zero is Monday, and an integer for the total days in the month. Construct a markdown table for the calendar. Start with a header line containing Monday through Sunday separated by pipe characters. Add a second line for alignment containing hyphens and pipes. Loop from one to the total days. Prepend blank spaces separated by pipes for the days before the starting weekday. Insert the day numbers separated by pipes. Add newline characters at the end of each seven day week. Return the full markdown string representing the monthly calendar grid. For example, start one and days thirty should place day one under Tuesday and format a full markdown grid.

title: Customer Support Email Templates
spec: Develop a function `email(requests)` that takes a list of arrays containing a customer name, an action type word, and a product name. Generate full email bodies. If the action is welcome, the text should be dear name, welcome to our platform. If the action is password, the text should be dear name, click here to reset your password. If the action is shipping, the text should be dear name, your product has shipped. If the action is review, the text should be dear name, please leave a review for product. Join all the email bodies together with a separator line made of ten dash characters and return the single combined string.

title: System Metrics Report
spec: Implement a function `report(stats)` that accepts a list of arrays holding a server name, a cpu utilization number, and a memory usage number. Generate a plain text diagnostic report. Start the string with the title SYSTEM STATUS REPORT followed by a newline and ten equals signs. Loop through the servers. If the cpu is over ninety, use the label CRITICAL. If it is over seventy, use WARNING. Otherwise, use NORMAL. Format each line as the server name followed by a colon and a space, the status label, a comma and space, the cpu number with a percent sign, and the memory number with the letters MB appended. Return the single formatted report string. For example, server alpha with cpu ninety five and memory two thousand should produce a line saying alpha: CRITICAL, 95%, 2000MB.

title: Game Scoreboard Formatter
spec: Create a function `scoreboard(players)` that receives a list of arrays with a player name and their score, which is already sorted from highest to lowest. Create an ascii scoreboard text block. The very first line should be the phrase TOP SCORES enclosed in asterisks. For the first player in the list, prefix their name with the phrase GOLD MEDAL. For the second player, prefix with SILVER MEDAL. For the third, prefix with BRONZE MEDAL. For the fourth and fifth players, prefix with HONORABLE MENTION. For all others, prefix with the word RANK and their index number. Suffix every player line with a space, a hyphen, a space, and their score points. Return a list of these formatted string lines.

title: Workout Planner
spec: Write a function `workout(routines)` that takes a list of arrays where each array has a day name, an activity type word, and an exercise name. Build a weekly schedule string. For each entry, if the activity type is rest, output the day name followed by a colon, a space, and the phrase take a day off. If the type is cardio, output the day name, a colon, the exercise name, and the phrase keep your heart rate up. If the type is strength, output the day name, a colon, the exercise name, and the phrase lift heavy. If the type is flexibility, output the day name, a colon, the exercise name, and the phrase stretch deeply. If the type is balance, output the day name, a colon, the exercise name, and the phrase stay focused. Separate each day line with a newline character and return the full string.

title: Travel Itinerary Formatter
spec: Develop a function `itinerary(events)` that accepts a list of arrays containing a day number, an event type word, and a location string. Build a readable travel text guide. If the event type is flight, format the line as Day number followed by a colon and the phrase Departure flight from location. If it is hotel, format as Day number, a colon, and Check into hotel at location. If it is tour, format as Day number, a colon, and Guided tour of location. If it is meal, format as Day number, a colon, and Dinner reservation at location. End the guide by appending a final line with the exact phrase END OF TRIP. Return a list of all the formatted strings.

title: Command Line Help Generator
spec: Implement a function `help(flags)` that takes a list of arrays containing a short flag letter, a long flag word, a text description, and a default value. Create a terminal help menu layout. Start the string with the word USAGE followed by a space and the word options. For each flag, create a line with two spaces, a hyphen, the short flag, a comma and space, two hyphens, the long flag, a space, and then the description. If the default value is not null, append a space, an open bracket, the word default followed by a colon and space, the default value, and a close bracket. Return the complete text block containing all lines joined by newlines.

title: Podcast Feed XML Builder
spec: Create a function `podcast(episodes)` that accepts a list of arrays containing an episode title, a duration string, and a date string. Construct a basic RSS feed XML document as a single string. Start with an open rss tag and an open channel tag. For each episode, append an open item tag. Inside, append an open title tag with the title and a close title tag, an open duration tag with the duration and a close duration tag, and an open pubDate tag with the date and a close pubDate tag. Then append a close item tag. After processing all episodes, append a close channel tag and a close rss tag. Return the combined XML string.

title: Stock Portfolio Summary
spec: Write a function `portfolio(stocks)` that takes a list of arrays with a stock ticker symbol, a buy price, and a current price. Create a text summary of the investments. Start the output with the phrase PORTFOLIO SUMMARY followed by a newline. For each stock, calculate the difference between current and buy price. If the current price is higher, format the line as the ticker symbol, a space, the word UP, a space, the word PROFIT, and the difference. If lower, format as ticker, space, DOWN, space, LOSS, and the absolute difference. If exactly equal, format as ticker, space, FLAT, space, BREAKEVEN. Return the lines as a single string joined by newline characters.

title: Quiz Flashcard Printer
spec: Develop a function `flashcards(questions)` that accepts a list of arrays containing a subject category, a question string, and an answer string. Generate a text file layout for printing flashcards. Start the entire document with the phrase FLASHCARD DECK and a newline. For each item, if the category is math, prefix the question with the phrase MATH CALCULATION and a colon. If the category is history, prefix with HISTORICAL FACT and a colon. If science, prefix with SCIENTIFIC CONCEPT and a colon. If literature, prefix with LITERARY QUOTE and a colon. After the question, append a newline, the phrase ANSWER with a colon, the actual answer, and a line of ten underscores. Return the full text block.

title: Guitar Tab Formatter
spec: Implement a function `lyrics(chords)` that takes a list of basic chord name strings. Translate these into a text document showing the specific finger placements. Map the chord C to the string x three two zero one zero. Map the chord G to three two zero zero zero three. Map the chord D to x x zero two three two. Map Am to x zero two two one zero. Map E to zero two two one zero zero. Start the output string with the title GUITAR CHORDS followed by two newlines. Then for each chord in the list, output the chord name, a space, an equals sign, a space, and the mapped finger placement string, separated by newlines. Return the complete string. For example, a list containing C and G should output the title, then C = x32010, and G = 320003 on separate lines.

title: Recipe Ingredients Markdown
spec: Create a function `recipe(ingredients)` that receives a list of arrays with a quantity number, a unit word, and an ingredient name. Convert the list into a markdown checklist. If the unit is grams, replace it with the letter g. If kilograms, replace with kg. If milliliters, replace with ml. If liters, replace with the uppercase letter L. If pieces, replace it with an empty string so no unit is shown. Format each line starting with a hyphen, a space, an open square bracket, a space, a close square bracket, a space, the quantity, the modified unit, a space, and the ingredient name. Return an array of these formatted markdown string lines.

title: Board Game Setup Instructions
spec: Write a function `setup(players)` that takes an integer representing the number of people playing a board game. Generate a step by step setup text guide. The first step should always be the phrase Step one: Place the main board in the center of the table. The second step should be Step two: Shuffle the encounter deck and deal three cards. If the number of players is two, the third step is Step three: Give each player fifty gold coins and two tokens. If the players are three, the third step is Step three: Give each player forty gold coins and three tokens. If four, the step is Step three: Give each player thirty gold coins and four tokens. Return a list of these exact instruction strings. For example, an input of three should return a list containing the generic step one, the generic step two, and the specific step three for three players.

title: Submarine Depth Zones
spec: Write a function `locate(depths)` that takes a list of depth values in meters. Return a list of zone classifications. For a depth less than zero, the zone is above sea level. For exactly zero, the zone is ocean surface. For less than two hundred, the zone is epipelagic. For less than one thousand, it is mesopelagic. For less than four thousand, it is bathypelagic. For less than six thousand, it is abyssopelagic. For less than ten thousand, it is hadalpelagic. Anything deeper is trench bottom. Example: an input of fifty results in epipelagic.

title: Train Ticket Categories
spec: Write a function `price(passengers)` taking a list of passenger ages in years. Determine their ticket category and return a list of results. If age is less than zero, it is an invalid age. If under two, it is infant lap. If under five, it is toddler seat. If under thirteen, it is child fare. If under eighteen, it is youth fare. If under sixty five, it is standard adult. If under eighty, it is senior discount. Eighty or over is elder free pass. Example: an input of sixty seven results in senior discount.

title: Soil Acidity Levels
spec: Write a function `analyze(levels)` that processes a list of soil pH numbers and returns a list of acidity descriptions. If the pH is less than four point five, it is extremely acid. If less than five point one, it is very strongly acid. If less than five point six, it is strongly acid. If less than six point one, it is moderately acid. If less than six point six, it is slightly acid. If less than seven point four, it is neutral soil. If less than seven point nine, it is slightly alkaline. If less than eight point five, it is moderately alkaline. Anything higher is strongly alkaline. Example: an input of seven results in neutral soil.

title: Paper Weight Classes
spec: Write a function `weigh(grams)` that processes a list of paper weights in grams per square meter and returns a list of types. Less than thirty five is tissue paper. Less than fifty five is newsprint paper. Less than ninety is text paper. Less than one hundred twenty is heavy text. Less than one hundred fifty is light cardstock. Less than two hundred is medium cardstock. Less than three hundred is heavyweight cover. Anything heavier is rigid board. Example: an input of forty results in newsprint paper.

title: Sound Intensity Levels
spec: Write a function `assess(decibels)` evaluating a list of sound levels and returning a list of descriptions. Below twenty is silent room. Below forty is quiet whisper. Below sixty is normal conversation. Below eighty is city traffic. Below one hundred is noisy factory. Below one hundred twenty is live concert. Below one hundred forty is pain threshold. Anything higher is hearing damage. Example: an input of seventy results in city traffic.

title: Avalanche Danger Scale
spec: Write a function `warn(dangers)` that takes a list of avalanche danger scores and returns a list of warning levels. If the score is less than zero, it is an invalid reading. If exactly zero, it is no data. If one, it is low danger. If two, it is moderate danger. If three, it is considerable danger. If four, it is high danger. If five, it is extreme danger. Anything higher is sensor error. Example: an input of three results in considerable danger.

title: Coffee Roasting Stages
spec: Write a function `roast(temperatures)` taking bean temperatures in Celsius and returning a list of stages. Below one hundred sixty five is drying phase. Below one hundred ninety six is cinnamon roast. Below two hundred five is new england roast. Below two hundred ten is american roast. Below two hundred nineteen is city roast. Below two hundred twenty five is full city roast. Below two hundred thirty is vienna roast. Below two hundred forty five is french roast. Anything higher is burnt carbon. Example: an input of two hundred results in new england roast.

title: Electric Vehicle Battery Charge
spec: Write a function `charge(percentages)` taking a list of battery levels and returning a list of statuses. Below five is critical empty. Below fifteen is low warning. Below thirty is needs charging. Below fifty is below half. Below eighty is healthy range. Below ninety five is almost full. Below one hundred is topping off. Exactly one hundred is fully charged. Anything higher is sensor error. Example: an input of twenty results in needs charging.

title: Water Salinity Grades
spec: Write a function `test(salinities)` for a list of water salinity levels in parts per thousand, returning a list of classifications. Less than zero point five is fresh water. Less than five is oligohaline water. Less than eighteen is mesohaline water. Less than thirty is polyhaline water. Less than forty is euhaline water. Less than fifty is hypersaline water. Less than one hundred is extreme brine. Anything higher is saturated salt. Example: an input of thirty five results in euhaline water.

title: Sunscreen UV Index
spec: Write a function `protect(indices)` that takes a list of UV index values and returns a list of risk levels. Less than three is low risk. Less than six is moderate risk. Less than eight is high risk. Less than eleven is very high risk. Less than fifteen is extreme risk. Less than twenty is danger level. Less than twenty five is shelter indoors. Anything higher is sensor malfunction. Example: an input of four results in moderate risk.

title: Bicycle Gear Ratios
spec: Write a function `pedal(ratios)` taking a list of bicycle gear ratios and returning a list of descriptions. Less than one is granny gear. Less than one point five is climbing gear. Less than two is easy cruising. Less than two point five is moderate pace. Less than three is fast flat. Less than three point five is sprinting gear. Less than four is downhill speed. Anything higher is track sprint. Example: an input of one point two results in climbing gear.

title: Pillow Loft Heights
spec: Write a function `sleep(lofts)` processing a list of pillow loft heights in inches and returning a list of profiles. Less than two is ultra thin. Less than three is low loft. Less than four is medium low. Less than five is medium loft. Less than six is medium high. Less than seven is high loft. Less than eight is extra high. Anything higher is wedge support. Example: an input of four point five results in medium loft.

title: Firewood Burning Heat
spec: Write a function `burn(btus)` that classifies a list of firewood heat outputs in millions of BTUs per cord, returning a list of classifications. Less than fifteen is low heat. Less than seventeen is fair heat. Less than nineteen is moderate heat. Less than twenty one is good heat. Less than twenty four is high heat. Less than twenty six is very high heat. Less than twenty eight is excellent heat. Anything higher is premium extreme heat. Example: an input of twenty results in good heat.

title: Hard Drive Rotation Speeds
spec: Write a function `spin(rpms)` for a list of hard drive speeds, returning a list of drive classes. Less than four thousand is eco drive. Less than five thousand is quiet storage. Less than six thousand is standard desktop. Less than seven thousand is performance desktop. Less than eight thousand is entry server. Less than eleven thousand is enterprise performance. Less than sixteen thousand is ultra high speed. Anything higher is experimental drive. Example: an input of five thousand four hundred results in standard desktop.

title: Printing Resolution Quality
spec: Write a function `print(dpis)` processing a list of image resolutions in dots per inch, returning a list of quality grades. Less than seventy two is low web quality. Less than one hundred fifty is draft print. Less than two hundred is standard office. Less than three hundred is high quality text. Less than six hundred is basic photo. Less than twelve hundred is professional photo. Less than twenty four hundred is fine art print. Anything higher is archival microprint. Example: an input of two hundred fifty results in high quality text.

title: Typing Speed Levels
spec: Write a function `type(wpms)` assessing a list of typing speeds in words per minute and returning a list of speed categories. Less than twenty is hunt and peck. Less than thirty is casual typist. Less than forty is average office. Less than fifty is productive typist. Less than sixty is fast professional. Less than eighty is highly advanced. Less than one hundred is competitive speed. Anything higher is elite level. Example: an input of forty five results in productive typist.

title: Video Game Frame Rates
spec: Write a function `render(fps)` that takes a list of frame rates and returns a list of experiences. Less than fifteen is unplayable slide show. Less than twenty four is cinematic low. Less than thirty is console standard. Less than forty five is smooth variable. Less than sixty is optimal standard. Less than ninety is high refresh. Less than one hundred twenty is competitive smooth. Anything higher is ultra enthusiast. Example: an input of sixty results in high refresh.

title: Internet Connection Speeds
spec: Write a function `connect(megabits)` for internet speeds in Mbps, returning a list of connection classes. Less than one is dial up era. Less than five is basic dsl. Less than twenty five is standard broadband. Less than one hundred is fast cable. Less than three hundred is ultra fast. Less than five hundred is half gigabit. Less than one thousand is gigabit fiber. Anything higher is multi gigabit. Example: an input of fifty results in fast cable.

title: Exercise Heart Rate Zones
spec: Write a function `train(beats)` analyzing a list of heart rates and returning a list of training zones. Less than sixty is resting state. Less than eighty is warm up zone. Less than one hundred is fitness fat burn. Less than one hundred twenty is aerobic steady. Less than one hundred forty is anaerobic threshold. Less than one hundred sixty is peak performance. Less than one hundred eighty is maximum effort. Anything higher is danger zone. Example: an input of one hundred ten results in aerobic steady.

title: Mountain Peak Altitudes
spec: Write a function `climb(meters)` evaluating a list of mountain heights and returning a list of classifications. Less than one thousand is low hill. Less than two thousand is moderate peak. Less than three thousand is high mountain. Less than four thousand is very high altitude. Less than five thousand is extreme altitude. Less than six thousand is thin air zone. Less than seven thousand is death zone border. Anything higher is true death zone. Example: an input of two thousand five hundred results in high mountain.

title: Plant Hardiness Zones
spec: Write a function `grow(temps)` for a list of minimum temperatures in Fahrenheit, returning a list of zone descriptions. Less than negative forty is zone one extreme cold. Less than negative thirty is zone two subarctic. Less than negative twenty is zone three cold continental. Less than negative ten is zone four chilly. Less than zero is zone five moderate winter. Less than ten is zone six mild winter. Less than twenty is zone seven temperate. Anything higher is zone eight warm. Example: an input of negative fifteen results in zone three cold continental.

title: Credit Score Ranges
spec: Write a function `lend(scores)` for a list of credit scores, returning a list of rating descriptions. Less than five hundred is deep subprime. Less than five hundred eighty is poor credit. Less than six hundred twenty is fair credit. Less than six hundred sixty is moderate risk. Less than seven hundred is good credit. Less than seven hundred forty is very good standing. Less than eight hundred is excellent history. Anything higher is exceptional credit. Example: an input of six hundred eighty results in good credit.

title: Diving Oxygen Toxicity
spec: Write a function `dive(pressures)` that takes a list of partial pressures of oxygen and returns a list of exposure warnings. Less than zero point sixteen is hypoxic hazard. Less than zero point two is mild hypoxia. Less than zero point five is normal safe range. Less than one point zero is enriched safe. Less than one point two is high working limit. Less than one point four is absolute maximum. Less than one point six is extreme danger. Anything higher is acute toxicity. Example: an input of one point three results in absolute maximum.

title: Refrigerator Temperature Zones
spec: Write a function `chill(celsius)` for a list of temperatures, returning a list of storage zones. Less than negative eighteen is deep freeze. Less than negative five is soft freeze. Less than zero is icy chill. Less than two is raw meat safe. Less than four is optimal fridge. Less than seven is dairy safe. Less than ten is produce crisper. Anything higher is unsafe warm. Example: an input of three results in optimal fridge.
